entries.name: Rakka
entries.look: Rakka is a mysterious figure who employs agents for dangerous retrieval missions from a hidden temple deep in the enchanted woods. Archie Miser worked for Rakka in the period leading up to the Swiftsoul incident, receiving payments for 'retrieval fees' and 'courier services.' Rakka may be connected to the teleportation that brought Archie to Swiftsoul, and the phrase 'Rakka silence protocol' in Archie's ledger suggests their relationship may have become dangerous. entries.name: Red
entries.look:
The commander in the manor kitchen. The guards describe her as the heir's greatest soldier and warn that she will eat you alive like the monsters will. She is not fighting the plants. She is feeding them, and what she feeds them makes them wither in the hand. Two guards holding a door shut said her name before they said what was behind them, which is its own kind of testimony. *A commander, Red - he, she - is preparing the dinner. She will eat you alive like the monsters. She's the heir's greatest soldier.*

entries.name: The Hallway Guard
entries.look:
A house guard left holding a corridor, and the only witness in the manor to notice that the reinforcements who died in it were not killed by plants. They had sword slashes. He is also the man who suggested putting the kitchen's soup inside a bomb, which is the best tactical idea anybody has had in this house. He was guarding a hallway. He is still guarding the hallway. Asked what happened to the reinforcements, he answered without dressing it up: they died.

Then he said the part that matters, and said it as though it were an ordinary detail rather than the single most important sentence filed

entries.name: The Mushroom Room Guard
entries.look:
A house guard who maintains that the mushroom room had no effect on him whatsoever, and who was missing for a stretch of time he accounts for as field observations. His eyes are bloodshot. The mushrooms, when picked up and sniffed, are fine. He is the manor's least reliable witness and its most useful one, because the shape of what he gets wrong is informative.
